YCS Montréal kicked off yesterday with the Genesys Main Event. Duelists battled it out in 7 Swiss Rounds, competing to secure a spot in Sunday’s Top 64 of the Genesys Main Event. Today, 739 registered Duelists will start over in a brand new tournament – the Advanced Main Event!

Today’s tournament will use the Advanced Format Forbidden & Limited List. Unlike Duels played in the Genesys Format, the Advanced Format permits Duelists to use every Summoning mechanic available, including Link Summoning and Pendulum Summoning. In addition, since there are no point restrictions placed on Deckbuilding, Decks that players use to compete are generally stronger and more capable of taking decisive victories.

Kewl Tune Decks appeared to dominate the Advanced Format at the recent North America World Championship Qualifier, but Ryan Yu’s Sky Striker Deck ultimately took home the trophy. Lots of Decks using the new cards based around
saw some success as well, which is likely to inspire more Duelists to experiment with that recent theme from
. In addition, the new

, which were just released on August 7th, include cards that bolster the Lunalight, Speedroid, and Odd-Eyes themes. We’ll find out this weekend whether the new cards in these themes will be enough to allow Decks built around them to compete with top contenders in the Advanced Format. We’ll also find out whether Decks that prevailed at the 2026 North America World Championship Qualifier will continue to succeed or new strategies will emerge as dominant.

A new season of Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series (“YCS”) Dueling begins this weekend! YCS Montréal is the first YCS in North America since the North America World Championship Qualifier took place last month, and it kicks off a new normal for YCS events! Starting this weekend, North America’s YCS events feature

, with two separate tournaments taking place! A Genesys Main Event kicks off on Friday, an Advanced Main Event begins on Saturday, and top-placing competitors from both events will battle it out on Sunday to determine the champion of each tournament. We’ll be bringing written coverage of the events to the blog all weekend, starting with today’s Genesys Format tournament play!

In addition to the new Genesys gameplay that is now a mainstay of the extended YCS weekend, YCS Montréal brings Duelists new prizing that competitors can’t wait to get their hands on! A brand new trophy and various new prize cards are available for the first time this weekend, in addition to other never-before-seen prizes. Follow the blog coverage throughout the weekend to get a glimpse of the new prizing.

The three-day YCS structure and exclusive YCS prizing aren’t the only features that are new this weekend. The Genesys competition kicking off today has a new Genesys Format Points Update in effect, tweaking the Genesys Format that we saw at the North America World Championship Qualifier in July. Blitzclique Decks dominated the Genesys Format Main Event at the North America WCQ, with 7 Blitzclique Decks making it into the Top 8. The latest update adds points to several cards commonly used in Blitzclique Decks, potentially altering the landscape of the competitive Genesys Format. Various other point changes will also affect which Decks Duelists use to compete in the Genesys Format Main Event this weekend.
In the Advanced Format Main Event kicking off tomorrow, a few new cards are entering the fray!
is still the most recently released core booster set, and the cards it contains – including
and cards in the “Light and Darkness Ritual” theme – are likely to have a big impact this weekend, just like they did at the North America World Championship Qualifier. But the

Decks released just a week ago introduce new cards that boost Lunalight, Odd-Eyes, and Speedroid Decks. In the hands of strong Duelists, these new cards could help their respective themes reach a new competitive level.
An exciting three days of Dueling are ahead! 139 Duelists are now seated to begin competing in the Genesys Format Main Event, and the tournament is about to start! It’s almost time to Duel!

r.b: Q: Where is YCS Montréal, QC?

r:
A: YCS Montréal, QC 2026 will be held at:

Montréal Convention Centre
Société du Palais des Congrès de Montréal
Hall 220 AB
1001 Pl. Jean-Paul-Riopelle
Montréal, QC H2Y 0A3
Canada

r.b: Q: What is the attendance capacity for this YCS?

r: Due to safety, health, and fire regulations, we have seating for up to 800 Duelists for this YCS (this is the total Duelist venue capacity). We urge you to pre-register online to have a better chance of being able to play in the Main Events. If the venue reaches capacity, additional Duelists will not be allowed to enter the hall. As space opens up from the Main Events, we will offer numerous Public Events that you will still be able to participate in throughout the weekend.

r.b: Q: How many Main Events will be at YCS Montréal, QC?

r: YCS Montréal, QC will feature two Main Events. The Genesys Main Event Day 1 will be held on Friday, August 14
and Day 2 on Sunday, August 16
. The Advanced Main Event Day 1 will be held on Saturday, August 15
and Day 2 on Sunday, August 16
. If a Duelist makes Day 2 for both events, they will need to choose which Day 2 they want to compete in once the standings are posted at the end of Saturday, August 16

r.b: Q: What are the Deck-building requirements for the Main Events?

r: Duelists can find detailed information about Deck-building for Advanced and Genesys on the Deck construction page, https://www.yugioh-card.com/en/limited/
Here is the basic information:
Decks must follow the Forbidden & Limited List, which can be viewed at https://www.yugioh-card.com/en/limited/list_2026-05-18/
For information on how to submit your Advanced Deck List, please see

r.b: When do I turn in my Deck List for the Advanced Main Event?

r: Genesys rules are simple:
No Link Monsters or Pendulum Monsters are allowed. All other cards are allowed. The original field layout is used, with no Extra Monster Zones nor Pendulum Zones.
The standard Forbidden & Limited Cards list is not used. All those cards can be used, except Link Monsters and Pendulum Monsters. Usual limit of 3 copies max of any card still applies.

Deck construction uses a point system. Some cards are assigned a point value; most cards cost zero points. The total point cost of cards in your Main Deck, Extra Deck, and Side Deck (combined) cannot exceed the point cap for that event.

For the Genesys Main Event, we will use the 100 Points cap for Deck-building. Click the link below for the current Genesys Points list. Genesys Deck List must be submitted through NEURON, the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG support app.
https://www.yugioh-card.com/en/genesys
For information on how to submit your Genesys Deck List, please see

r.b: How do I turn in my Deck List for the Genesys Main Event?
Q: How many Rounds will the Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series have?

r: The total number of Duelists in each of the Main Events, Advanced and Genesys, will determine the number of Rounds that are played in that specific Main Event.

r.b: Q: How many Duelists will advance to Day 2?

r: If there are 256 or fewer Duelists registered for one of the Main Events, Advanced or Genesys, then the Top 64 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 15 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2 for that specific Main Event.

If there are 257 – 512 Duelists registered for one of the Main Events, Advanced or Genesys, then the Top 64 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 18 points, whichever is larger, will advance to Day 2 for that specific Main Event.

If there are 513 – 1024 Duelists registered for one of the Main Events, Advanced or Genesys, then the Top 128 Duelists OR all Duelists with a minimum of 18 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2 for that specific Main Event.

r.b: Q: What cards are legal for play?

r: Please check the “Products” page online at https://www.yugioh‐card.com/en/products/ for the most current legality dates of Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME product releases, prior to preparing your Deck for the event.
Cards that have been altered from their original appearance with surface decoration may be used for play
only if the alterations do not obscure any portion of the card text, make the illustration difficult to recognize, or make the card distinguishable from other cards in the Deck while it is face-down.
If a card’s surface decoration renders the card unrecognizable at first glance, then the card is not allowed for tournament play.

The Head Judge of the event has final arbitration on whether or not altered cards may be used at the tournament. Duelists are responsible for determining whether or not their altered cards are acceptable for use before the start of the tournament.

r.b: Q: Will there be meal breaks during the YCS?

r: A: As there will be food and drinks available inside the tournament hall, there will not be any meal breaks scheduled into the tournament.

r.b: Q: Do I need a visa to enter Canada if I am from a different country?

r: A: Travelers to Canada may require a visa.
Residents of the United States do not need a visa to travel to Canada.

Residents of most European countries do not need a visa to travel to Canada but do require Electronic Travel Authorization. You can learn more about an Electronic Travel Authorization and apply for it on the Canadian government’s website at https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta.html
Residents of most Latin American countries do not require a visa if they have held a Canadian visa in the past 10 years.
For those that have held a Canadian visa in the past 10 years, an Electronic Travel Authorization is needed instead.
For those that have not held a Canadian visa in the past 10 years, a visa is required.
Residents of other locations will require a visa.

This information is accurate as of the time this FAQ was created. However, this information can change. If you are travelling to Canada from another country, please verify visa requirements before booking travel to ensure requirements have not changed.
